openPorts.attackType: Cleartext Credential Eavesdropping & IoT Botnet Takeover
openPorts.exploitTarget: Cleartext credential eavesdropping, Mirai IoT botnet propagation
openPorts.mitigation: Disable Telnet daemon completely. Migrate to SSH (Port 22) with key authentication.

Change default manufacturer credentials on all network routers and switches.

openPorts.attackType: Automated Dictionary / Brute-Force Scanning
openPorts.exploitTarget: Automated dictionary / brute-force scanning
openPorts.mitigation: Enforce public key authentication only, disable root login, deploy Fail2ban.
remediationSteps: Disable password authentication (PasswordAuthentication no) in sshd_config.
Disable direct root login (PermitRootLogin no).
Deploy Fail2ban or CrowdSec to automatically drop brute-forcing IPs.

firewallCmd.linuxIptables: sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m state --state NEW -m recent --set -j ACCEPT

openPorts.attackType: Man-in-the-Middle Credential Interception

openPorts.mitigation: Redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS (Port 443) and implement HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS).
remediationSteps: Configure web server to redirect 100% of HTTP traffic to HTTPS.
Deploy HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) header with max-age=31536000.

openPorts.attackType: Encrypted Web Communications (Monitor Web App Layer)
openPorts.exploitTarget: Web application vulnerabilities (SQLi, XSS) - Port itself is secure
openPorts.mitigation: Keep web application libraries patched and enforce TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites.
remediationSteps: Ensure TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 are enabled while deprecating SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1.
Maintain automated renewal of valid SSL/TLS certificates.

firewallCmd.powershell: # Port 443 is typically required for encrypted web traffic
